title: COS 101 ( UNINIGER ) : BRIEF HISTORY AND BASIC COMPONENTS OF COMPUTING DEVICE
subject: COS 101

questions.question: Blaise Pascal invented which gear-driven calculator in 1642?
questions.explanation: Blaise Pascal invented the Pascaline in 1642 as an aid for his father.

questions.question: The Jacquard Loom used which type of cards to weave fabric designs automatically?
questions.explanation: The Jacquard Loom used punched wooden cards to weave fabric designs automatically.

questions.question: Who is recognized as the world's first computer programmer?
questions.explanation: Ada Lovelace wrote programs for Babbage's Analytic Engine, making her the first computer programmer.

questions.question: Which invention by Charles Babbage was a steam-driven calculating machine?
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage proposed the Difference Engine, a steam-driven calculating machine.

questions.question: Herman Hollerith developed a punch-card system for which purpose?
questions.explanation: Herman Hollerith developed a punch-card system that helped calculate the 1890 U.S. Census.

questions.question: Which device was the first digital electronic computer in the U.S.?
questions.explanation: The Atanasoff-Berry Computer (ABC) was the first digital electronic computer in the U.S.

questions.question: ENIAC is an acronym for which of the following?
questions.explanation: ENIAC stands for Electronic Numerical Integrator and Calculator.

questions.question: Which computer was the first commercial computer for business and government applications?
questions.explanation: UNIVAC or Universal Automatic Computer was the first commercial computer.

questions.question: Grace Hopper is credited with developing which first computer programming language?
questions.explanation: Grace Hopper developed COBOL, which was the first computer programming language.

questions.question: The UNIX operating system was developed in 1969 by developers at which location?
questions.explanation: Ken Thompson and other developers at Bell Lab developed UNIX in 1969.

questions.question: The ENIAC was invented by which two university professors?
questions.explanation: John Mauchly and J. Presper Eckert invented the ENIAC.

questions.question: The first generation of computers was based on which technology?
questions.explanation: The first generation of computers (1945-1956) was based on vacuum tubes.

questions.question: Which programming language was used by first-generation computers?
questions.explanation: First-generation computers relied on machine language, the lowest-level programming language.

questions.question: First-generation computers could solve how many problems at a time?
questions.explanation: First-generation computers could only solve one problem at a time.

questions.question: Input for first-generation computers was based on which medium?
questions.explanation: The input for first-generation computers was based on punched cards and paper tape.

questions.question: The second generation of computers was based on which technology?
questions.explanation: The second generation of computers (1956-1963) was based on transistors.

questions.question: Each transistor in the second generation replaced the equivalent of how many vacuum tubes?
questions.explanation: Each transistor replaced the equivalent of 40 vacuum tubes.

questions.question: Second-generation computers moved from magnetic drums to which technology?
questions.explanation: Second-generation computers moved from a magnetic drum to magnetic core technology.

questions.question: The second generation of computers saw the development of early versions of which languages?
questions.explanation: High-level programming languages such as early versions of COBOL and FORTRAN were developed in the second generation.

questions.question: The third generation of computers was based on which technology?
questions.explanation: The third generation of computers (1964-1971) was based on integrated circuits.

questions.question: Third-generation computers allowed users to interact through which devices?
questions.explanation: Third-generation computers allowed interaction through keyboards and monitors.

questions.question: Third-generation computers reduced costs considerably because transistors were miniaturized onto what?
questions.explanation: Transistors were miniaturized and placed on silicon chips, called semiconductors.

questions.question: The fourth generation of computers is based on which technology?
questions.explanation: The fourth generation of computers (1971-present) is based on the microprocessor.

questions.question: Monolithic integrated circuits used in fourth-generation computers put millions of transistors onto how many chips?
questions.explanation: Monolithic integrated circuits put millions of transistors onto one integrated circuit chip.

questions.question: Fourth-generation microprocessors were available in which range of bit sizes?
questions.explanation: Fourth-generation microprocessors included 4-bit, 8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit, and 64-bit processors.

questions.question: The fifth generation of computers is based on which technologies?
questions.explanation: The fifth generation of computers is based on artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML).

questions.question: Which feature is associated with the fifth generation of computers?
questions.explanation: Parallel processing is a feature supported by fifth-generation computers.

questions.question: Artificial intelligence becoming a reality is expected to be helped by parallel processing and which other technology?
questions.explanation: It is believed that the use of parallel processing and superconductors will help to make artificial intelligence a reality.

questions.question: A computer is defined as an electronic device that performs which of the following?
questions.explanation: A computer accepts data, performs operations, displays results, and stores the data or results as needed.

questions.question: Which term refers to the physical components of a computer?
questions.explanation: Hardware is the physical components of a computer like a processor, memory devices, monitor, and keyboard.

questions.question: A set of programs or instructions required by hardware to function properly is called which term?
questions.explanation: Software is a set of programs or instructions required by the hardware resources to function properly.

questions.question: The course COS 101 is titled which of the following?
questions.explanation: The course is titled COS 101: Introduction to Computing Sciences.

questions.question: The input unit converts user input into which language for the computer to understand?
questions.explanation: Input devices take input and convert it into binary language that the computer understands.

questions.question: The input unit is formed by attaching which devices to a computer?
questions.explanation: The Input Unit is formed by attaching one or more input devices to a computer.

questions.question: The Central Processing Unit is often referred to as which part of the computer?
questions.explanation: The CPU is called the brain of the computer because it is the control centre.

questions.question: The CPU has three main components which include ALU, Control Unit, and which other unit?
questions.explanation: The CPU has three main components: Arithmetic Logic Unit, Control Unit, and Registers.

questions.question: The CPU fetches instructions from memory and then does which action?
questions.explanation: The CPU first fetches instructions from memory and then interprets them to know what is to be done.

questions.question: Arithmetic calculations like addition and subtraction are performed by which component?
questions.explanation: The ALU performs mathematical calculations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.

questions.question: Logical decisions involving comparison of two data items are performed by which component?
questions.explanation: The ALU takes logical decisions involving comparison of two data items.

questions.question: Which component coordinates and controls the data flow in and out of the CPU?
questions.explanation: The Control Unit coordinates and controls the data flow in and out of the CPU.

questions.question: The Control Unit sends control signals to which devices until the required operation is done?
questions.explanation: The Control Unit sends control signals to input/output devices until the required operation is done properly by ALU.

questions.question: Registers are described as high-speed devices for storing data or instructions in which manner?
questions.explanation: Registers are high-speed devices for storing data or instructions temporarily.

questions.question: The main register in the ALU that contains one of the operands is called which term?
questions.explanation: Accumulator (ACC) is the main register in the ALU and contains one of the operands.

questions.question: Registers can be of different sizes which include 16 bit, 32 bit, and which other size?
questions.explanation: Registers can be of different sizes such as 16 bit, 32 bit, and 64 bit.

questions.question: Internal memory is also known by which alternative name?
questions.explanation: The internal memory is also called the Primary memory or Main memory.

questions.question: Which type of memory is not immediately accessible to the computer?
questions.explanation: Memories that are not immediately accessible to the Computer is called secondary memory.

questions.question: Each memory location in internal memory is of the same size and has which property?
questions.explanation: Each memory location is of the same size and has an address.

questions.question: The output unit converts binary data coming from the CPU into which form?
questions.explanation: The output unit converts binary data coming from the CPU to human understandable form.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common output device?
questions.explanation: Monitor, printer, and plotter are common output devices.

questions.question: Which inventor proposed the Analytic Engine?
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage designed the Analytic Engine, a steam-driven calculating machine.
